short_summary: A Tel Aviv University study reveals that Israeli grocery prices rose nearly five times faster over the past four years than in the previous period. The findings highlight sharp retail price increases despite minimal growth in domestic production costs.

sources.name: Walla
sources.title: סיכום קדנציה מזעזע: מחירי המזון בישראל זינקו ב-19% בארבע שנים

paragraphs: For Israeli consumers pushing carts through supermarket aisles, escalating grocery receipts have transitioned from a nagging suspicion into documented reality. A comprehensive study conducted by Professor Itai Ater and doctoral researcher Adi Omer from Tel Aviv University’s Faculty of Management reveals that food prices surged nearly five times faster over the past four years than during the preceding four-year cycle.

Analyzing data gathered by the Pricez platform, the researchers tracked a basket of eighty staple goods across approximately seven hundred supermarket branches over an eight-year span. Between September 2022 and August 2026, this fixed grocery basket climbed by 19.6 percent in neighborhood grocers, 19 percent through online portals, and 14.5 percent across discount retail chains. By comparison, during the previous four-year period from 2018 to 2022, identical products registered modest price hikes of 4.3 percent, 4.1 percent, and 2.8 percent respectively.

Several individual pantry items experienced dramatic jumps. A standard one-hundred-gram bar of Elite milk chocolate soared by roughly 78 percent in local shops, jumping from 5.21 shekels to 9.26 shekels, while climbing 73.5 percent on the internet. An eight-hundred-gram package of Maadanot cheese bourekas spiked 47.5 percent digitally, reaching 22.76 shekels. Prices for Taster’s Choice coffee jumped 26.1 percent in neighborhood stores, and infant formula saw an increase of nearly 15 percent, reversing prior declines. Notable increases also struck goods like Hellmann’s mayonnaise, Nutella spread, and Sugat jasmine rice.

In absolute terms, the financial burden expanded considerably. At Shufersal Deal, the monitored basket increased by 231 shekels, compared to a mere six-shekel increase during the prior four years. Shufersal Sheli registered a 222-shekel jump, while Shufersal Online leaped by 247 shekels. Among discount chains, Rami Levy offered the least expensive basket, followed by Yohananof, whereas Tiv Taam and Shufersal Deal featured the priciest selections.

Crucially, the research uncovered a puzzling divergence between shelf prices and underlying production expenditures. Data from the Central Bureau of Statistics cited in the report indicated that the food manufacturing price index climbed by roughly 2 percent over the four-year window, compared to 12 percent previously. While municipal taxes, value-added tax adjustments, and utility tariffs exerted upward pressure, other economic indicators—such as a stronger shekel and falling global commodity prices from their 2022 zeniths—should theoretically have cushioned domestic expenses. A 2024 State Comptroller report had already highlighted that Israeli groceries were approximately 37 percent costlier than the OECD average.

The authors argued that governmental preoccupation with political turmoil and armed conflict sidelined cost-of-living concerns, allowing retail conglomerates to elevate price tags amidst diminished public scrutiny. Although food inflation decelerated to 1 percent annually by August 2026, prices remained entrenched at elevated plateaus. The resulting strain disproportionately punishes vulnerable households: families in the lowest income quintile allocate 18.5 percent of their monthly budget to groceries, compared with 12.3 percent among top earners. Ater emphasized that containing prices demands deliberate structural interventions, regulatory dismantling of import barriers, and robust antimonopoly enforcement.

facts.fact: A study by Prof. Itai Ater and Adi Omer of Tel Aviv University found that grocery prices in Israel rose nearly five times faster between September 2022 and August 2026 than in the preceding four years.
The study tracked a basket of 80 popular products across roughly 700 stores using Pricez data, showing increases of 19.6% in neighborhood shops, 19% online, and 14.5% in discount chains.
During the previous four-year period (2018–2022), prices for the same basket rose by 4.3% in neighborhood shops, 4.1% online, and 2.8% in discount chains.
Specific items saw steep hikes: Elite milk chocolate rose nearly 78% in neighborhood shops, Maadanot bourekas climbed 47.5% online, and Taster's Choice coffee rose 26.1% locally.
The price of the basket at Shufersal Deal increased by 231 shekels, compared with just 6 shekels in the previous four-year period.
The food manufacturing price index tracked by the Central Bureau of Statistics rose only about 2% over the four years, compared to 12% in the preceding period.
A 2024 State Comptroller report showed Israel's food basket was approximately 37% more expensive than the OECD average.
Food spending accounts for 18.5% of monthly household expenditure in Israel's lowest income quintile, compared to 12.3% in the highest quintile.
